subject: Temporary outbound-processing window & evidence request — residency clarification
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@healthtech.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthTech Legal <legal@healthtech.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick clarification on transient outbound-processing during APAC maintenance

Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, Legal has a couple of specific asks around the APAC deployment. Two quick items we need clarified before we proceed:

1) During unavoidable cross-region failover or upgrades, do you ever perform outbound processing that hops through non-APAC regions for brief windows ("transient egress")? If so, what's the maximum expected window and what controls are in place?

2) Can you provide evidence that such transient processing is logged and that KMS-wrapped keys / egress telemetry are auditable for post-event review? Legal mentioned they want a playback or sample export they can review.

If you can point to a sample artifact or schedule a short call with your security ops to walk through a record, that would speed things up.

Appreciate it —
Samir
Samir Patel
Security & Privacy Lead
HealthTech Inc.

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on transient outbound-processing during APAC maintenance

Samir —

Short answer: yes, in limited, controlled scenarios we may route ephemeral traffic outside APAC for brief failover/replication windows, but we treat them as security exceptions with strong telemetry and retention controls. I've attached a one-page summary of our residency playbook that outlines the maximum window we allow, the conditions under which this happens, and the guardrails.

Attachments: residency-playbook-summary.pdf (summary of transient-egress policy, max windows, and logging artifacts)

High level:
- Typical window: < 72 hours for operational failovers in extreme scenarios; common maintenance/restart windows are minutes-to-hours and we prefer warm standby inside region.
- Controls: KMS-wrapped key usage for ephemeral caches, path-based audit logs for any cross-hop, mandatory entry in the incident registry, and customer-level opt-in for temporary egress exceptions.
- Evidence: we can provide an "audit playback" export containing per-request region/hop traces, KMS key IDs used, and a redacted token-level timing trace.

I'll loop in our compliance lead and infra ops to prepare a sanitized sample for Legal. Marissa / Kimberly — can you confirm the earliest we can produce a 24–72h playback sample and a mapping of kms key paths for HealthTech's account?

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on transient outbound-processing during APAC maintenance

Michael / team —

Looping in Karthik for ops confirmation. Notes from infra: we can produce the requested artifacts but need to be explicit on scope so Legal gets a representative sample rather than a full PII-laden export. Proposed deliverables:

- Playback export (redacted): per-request region tag, timestamp, hop sequence, and KMS key ID. Redact any user payloads. Format: CSV + small JSON manifest.
- KMS path mapping: CSV listing customer key IDs bound to regions and vaults (kms-key-paths.csv).
- Timeline doc: brief timeline showing max observed windows historically and the policy threshold (we should avoid saying 72h as a hard SLA; present as an operational upper bound).

Operational constraints / ask: we will need a signed non-production data-handling attestation and a date for when Legal wants to review. We generally deliver a sanitized artifact within 3 business days once Legal confirms exact fields to redact.

Kimberly — can you own the redaction guidance and confirm any legal-prescribed fields for HealthTech? Karthik — confirm whether we can produce a sample with KV-cache lineage for one historical failover (we have an anonymized run from 2027-05-14).

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Director, Compliance Operations

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthtech.com>
Cc: HealthTech Legal <legal@healthtech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on transient outbound-processing during APAC maintenance

Samir —

Thanks for the clear asks. Next steps and what we'll deliver:

1) Sanitary playback export (sample) — contains per-request region tags, hop sequence, timestamp, and KMS key IDs; payloads redacted. Delivery ETA: Tue 29 Jun 2027 EOD. Attachment will be a zip with CSV + manifest (transient-egress-proof.zip).

2) KMS key path mapping (kms-key-paths.csv) — includes vault/region mapping and the key alias we used in the sample. This is a metadata-only file; no secrets included.

3) Short technical walk-through — we can schedule a 30-minute call with our infra ops and compliance to go over the export and answer Legal's redaction questions. Proposed slots: Wed 30 Jun 09:00–11:00 PT or Thu 01 Jul 14:00–16:00 PT. Please let us know what works.

A few clarifications up front that Legal usually asks about:
- We never persist unredacted customer payloads outside the pinned region except when a customer explicitly allows a temporary exception (we'll record the consent as part of the incident).
- All transient hops are accompanied by a recorded incident note and automated log export; that log export is what we're sharing in the sample.
- Default caching behavior prefers in-region warm standby and KV cache replay; cross-hop happens only if regional capacity or network partitions prevent in-region handling.

If Legal wants narrower scope in the sample (e.g., only 1-hop traces or only handshake telemetry), Kimberly and Marissa will tailor it.

Samir — if you can confirm the preferred review slot and whether HealthTech prefers a playback that includes a single historical event (2027-05-14 anonymized) or a synthesized example, we'll proceed accordingly.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs referenced in thread:
- residency-playbook-summary.pdf (one-page policy summary)
- transient-egress-proof.zip (sanitized playback export; ETA Tue 29 Jun)
- kms-key-paths.csv (metadata mapping of key IDs to region/vault)
